I was told to start giving my son allergens right around a year old in small amounts.

After talking to a nurse about it she was saying that most serious food allergies come from parents keeping their babies away from food allergens until it's too late. Which makes sense as most people I've met that are allergic to peanuts, eggs, ham, etc say they never had those items until they were in school.

For the most part our allergies are due to our own actions or lack of exposure. Its also extremely interesting to look at how people adapt to animal allergens in a home. I was raised without cats or dogs in the home and subsequently was allergic to them until I finally lived in a house with one. Now I can literally bury my face in a cat or a dog without any problems. Some animals take a couple exposures for my body to "learn" their allergen signatures.

I have a step brother that was the same way with cats and dogs. The allergic reactions went away because he had to deal with living with cats.
